activity_context.topic_title: Finding the Canonical Form of a Quadratic Form Using Orthogonal Transformations

feedback.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 6 & 0 \\ 6 & -12 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}],\,D=[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -15\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices given above.
Find an orthogonal matrix $P$ such that $x=Py$ defines the corresponding change of variables that reduces the quadratic form $Q(x)={x}^{T}\,Ax$ to the canonical (diagonal) form ${y}^{T}\,Dy.$
feedback.worked_solution:
Every quadratic form can be reduced to its canonical (diagonal) form using orthogonal transformations.

From the diagonal matrix $D,$ we deduce that the eigenvalues of the matrix $A$ are 

$\,$ ${\lambda }_{1}=3,\,$ ${\lambda }_{2}=0,\,$ and $\,{\lambda }_{3}=-15.$

Now, we need to find an eigenvector basis of $A.$ 

- For ${\lambda }_{1}=3,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-3I & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 6 & 0 \\ 6 & -12 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}]-3[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-6 & 6 & 0 \\ 6 & -15 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(A-3I)x=0$ gives the eigenvector ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$ Dividing ${v}_{1}$ by its norm $‖{v}_{1}‖=1,$ we get 

$$
\frac{{v}_{1}}{‖{v}_{1}‖}=\frac{1}{1}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

- For ${\lambda }_{2}=0,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-0I & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 6 & 0 \\ 6 & -12 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}]-0[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 6 & 0 \\ 6 & -12 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(A-0I)x=0$ gives the eigenvector ${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].$ Dividing ${v}_{2}$ by its norm $‖{v}_{2}‖=\sqrt{5},$ we get 

$$
\frac{{v}_{2}}{‖{v}_{2}‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].
$$

- For ${\lambda }_{3}=-15,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-(-15)I & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 6 & 0 \\ 6 & -12 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}]-(-15)[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}12 & 6 & 0 \\ 6 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 18\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(A-(-15)I)x=0$ gives the eigenvector ${v}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}].$ Dividing ${v}_{3}$ by its norm $‖{v}_{3}‖=\sqrt{5},$ we get 

$$
\frac{{v}_{3}}{‖{v}_{3}‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, we construct the orthogonal matrix $P$ in the usual way, and this gives us the following:

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}0 & \frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} & -\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} \\ 0 & \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} & \frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} \\ 1 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$
